key_insight: NeuroGRIP refines EEG graph connections with external clinical knowledge to make seizure diagnosis more accurate and more interpretable.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians get seizure predictions that are grounded in medically plausible brain-network relationships rather than purely data-driven patterns.
method: Builds a domain-specific knowledge graph from clinical guidelines using LLM-extracted biomedical entities and relations.
Aligns EEG node embeddings with the knowledge graph to form semantic queries.
Uses FAISS retrieval and confidence scoring to prune implausible edges from EEG graphs.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on TUSZ and CHB-MIT, where the abstract reports improved seizure detection accuracy and better interpretability.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality, completeness, and bias of the external knowledge base and retrieved relations.
paper_title: NeuroGRIP: Retrieval-Augmented Graph Refinement for Knowledge-Grounded EEG Seizure Diagnosis
